_notes: Demand tables tuned by the accepted cart balance study (8 October 2026). Calculated proposals; not yet checked in game. Keys starting with an underscore are notes; the loader ignores them.
_passersPerHour: Passers per hour at footfall 1.0, before the menu's appetite. Calibration knob for the whole model. Raised from 16 to 20 on 21 October 2026 after an AI playtest and playtester feedback showed carts and trucks earning too little.
_streetBaseline: Ordinary street traffic, added to independent area crowds. Lunch 1.0 keeps any pavement alive at midday. With passersPerHour 16 (before the 21 October 2026 raise to 20), two offices at 20 and 40 m plus a nightclub at 30 m gave about 65 passers/hour at a Midtown lunch (docs/balance/cart-economics.md, section 6). Night stays low. All neighbourhood, month, rain and promotion factors still apply. First values pending balance recalibration and an in-game check.
_dayparts: Start time of each daypart. Late runs past midnight; night (02 to 05) is the dead hours the design leaves out.
_areas: Footfall per daypart and a factor per day of the week. 1.0 is the reference footfall, not the average after tuning. Before 05:00 the previous day's factors apply. Independent area crowds add to the street baseline. Optional appetite factors are weighted by each area's contribution to footfall at this hour; the baseline and unlisted categories use factor 1.0. Optional per area: weekendFootfall replaces footfall on Saturday and Sunday (days still applies), seasons (missing seasons 1.0) and rain (1.0 when left out) scale that area's own crowd on top of the month, season and rain factors every passer has. Waterfront covers piers, the waterfront and tourist stretches placed by zones; parks have their own area. Transit has all seven dayparts and weekdays from the study.

areas._park: Parks (Peter, 14 October 2026), from the game's park areas (classifier parkarea, skatepark) and hand-drawn zones. Weekdays are quiet except a lunch bump of office workers on the benches (1.4, about half an office block's lunch); mornings are joggers and dog walkers (0.5). Weekends are the park's days: late morning to early evening, peaking in the afternoon at 2.8, a little under the waterfront's weekend 3.2 because a park is a destination for locals rather than tourists. Night is empty (parks close). Summer 1.3 and winter 0.35 on top of the month (a January Saturday park is 0.21 of July's); rain 0.4 on top of rain.footfall 0.5, since nobody sits in a wet park. Appetite: what people buy on a walk or a lawn, so ice cream, slushies and snacks (popcorn, cotton candy, corn) x2 or more, cold drinks x1.8, hot dogs and other fast food x1.2 (the classic park cart), coffee x1.2 (a takeaway on the morning walk, moderate, below the waterfront's 2.0), sit-down meals lower (pizza 0.6, street meal 0.8). Bakery stays 1.0.

_categories: Base appetite: the share of passers who want the category in that daypart. newCustomerWeight scales how much of that share comes as customers of its own; addOnFactor turns the rest into items added to other customers' orders. marketFloor (optional) is the lowest the game's market demand counts for the category's items.

categories._colddrinks: Drinks pass of 19 October 2026: a cart with only a drinks fridge must sell (an AI playtest's soda cart served nobody in 3.5 hours). Half the appetite comes as customers of their own, the afternoon peaks, and marketFloor 0.7 keeps nearby shops' soda from halving a cart's trade. Calculator, weekday in May: a cooler-only cart $76/$130/$227/$353 a day at poor/typical/good/best pitches where the game's market is 31; hot dog + cooler best route $2,062 (was $2,058).
categories._streetmeal: Kabobs and dumplings: a plated street meal. Lunch-led like fast food, below it, with a steady evening and late trade (halal night carts). Offices x1.2. docs/balance/new-foods.md.
categories._snacks: Popcorn, cotton candy, grilled corn: impulse snacks for people with time. Afternoon and evening, parks x2, cinema and theatre crowds x1.5, shoppers x1.3, offices x0.5. Summer 1.3, autumn 1.1, winter 0.6, rain 0.5.
categories._slushies: A cold treat bought for itself, shaped like ice cream: afternoon peak, parks x2, summer 1.6, winter 0.3, rain 0.4. Not cold drinks: as an add-on it would replace the cooler at twice the margin.

_menu: The menu's strongest category counts in full, each further category adds this share of its own.
_neighbourhoods: Keyed by the game's neighbourhood IDs. footfall scales every area; dayparts, days and seasons are optional factors (missing means 1.0) that stack with the month's footfall: the Hamptons' winter 0.5 times the winter months' 0.6 is 0.3. appetite rules multiply the listed categories, limited to the listed dayparts, days and seasons when given. A neighbourhood not listed here is neutral.
_calendar: The game has no climate seasons, so the mod runs its own calendar from the in-game day: day 1 is the first day of startMonth, and each month lasts daysPerMonth days.
_seasons: Appetite factors per season. Categories not listed stay at 1.0.
_market: The game's demand per product and neighbourhood (0 to 100) divided by 100, kept between floor and ceiling.
_classifier: Buildings and businesses within radiusMetres vote for area types; a vote counts in full at the spot and edgeWeight at the radius. A business type rule replaces its building's rule. Each area independently gets presence = 1 - exp(-votes / saturation), with no normalization or trimming. maxAreas remains accepted for compatibility but is ignored. With no votes the spot has no area crowd, only the street baseline; fallbackArea remains accepted but is no longer used. Venues reach high presence without reducing any other crowd. Zones set direct presences in [0,1]; override replaces the automatic result, add raises each presence to at least the zone value. Legacy additive zone share is accepted but ignored. Subway entrances are nearby places reported by the game side with building type subwayentrance and vote transit. Parks are reported the same way from the game's own park areas (the trigger volumes that give the player the walking-in-the-park happiness boost): building type parkarea, or skatepark for the skate park, at the distance to the area's edge (0 inside). Parks the game has no area for, the waterfront and tourist stretches come from zones.

classifier._coverage: Venue weights follow the accepted study tuning; the other shop, service and public-service weights remain draft values for playtesting. Empty businesses stay unclassified so the building type decides. buildingtype_special stays unclassified: it covers different uses with no single sensible area; a known business type decides, otherwise the classifier falls back.
classifier._saturation: 1.25 makes two unit-weight buildings at 20-40 m give presence 0.62-0.72 (0.674 at 20 and 40 m); two at the spot give 0.798. Further buildings approach 1 with diminishing returns.
